translations.source_sense_description: een blaasinstrument dat dwars op de lippen geblazen wordt

glosses: A kind of flyboat; a storeship.

A woodwind instrument consisting of a tube with a row of holes that produce sound through vibrations caused by air blown across the edge of the holes, often tuned by plugging one or more holes with a finger; the Western concert flute, a transverse side-blown flute of European origin.

examples.text: The breathing flute's ſoft notes are heard around, / And the ſhril trumpets mix their ſilver ſound; / The vaulted roofs vvith echoing muſic ring, / Theſe touch the vocal ſtops, and thoſe the trembling ſtring.
The group played huge drums placed overhead, along with flutes and a kotolike zither.
After another alternation of the two elements, there is a more playful episode, in which flute and bassoon take up the first element, with swooping glissando on the ondes Martenot.

glosses: A recorder, also a woodwind instrument.
A glass with a long, narrow bowl and a long stem, used for drinking wine, especially champagne.

examples.text:
These are champagne glasses, says Peggy.
No, I mean the tall ones, Jamie says.
You're thinking of flutes, says Peggy. These are coupes.

glosses: A lengthwise groove, such as one of the lengthwise grooves on a classical column, or a groove on a cutting tool (such as a drill bit, endmill, or reamer), which helps to form both a cutting edge and a channel through which chips can escape.
A semicylindrical vertical groove, as in a pillar, in plaited cloth, or in a rifle barrel to cut down the weight.
A long French bread roll, baguette.
An organ stop with a flute-like sound.
A shuttle in weaving tapestry etc.
To play on a flute.
To make a flutelike sound.

examples.text: The green turf was velvet underfoot. The blackbirds fluted in the hazels there.

glosses: To utter with a flutelike sound.

examples.text: “Oh, there's my precious Poppet,” said Phyllis, as a distant barking reached the ears. “He's asking for his dinner, the sweet little angel. All right, darling, Mother's coming,” she fluted, and buzzed off on the errand of mercy.

glosses: To form flutes or channels in (as in a column, a ruffle, etc.); to cut a semicylindrical vertical groove in (as in a pillar, etc.).

glosses: Nom générique des flûtes à embouchure libre dont le biseau est situé au milieu du corps de l’instrument et que l’on tient de travers, de manière latérale.
Nom courant des flûtes traversières classiques.

examples.text: Les Gymnopédies de Satie et les valses de Chopin seront pour moi à jamais attachées à elle, tout comme Bach l’est à mon père qui jouait de la flûte traversière.
Il sera ensuite temps de se détendre autour d’un concert en plein air avec le duo baroque composé de Clémence Schweyer, au clavecin, et de Guillaume Handel, à la flûte traversière.
Andréa, flûte traversière et voix, accompagnée par Richard Heaney, à la guitare et voix mais aussi du percutrum barytar.
